text:
Toronto and Calgary arrive on the same 4-1-0 run, but they got there differently. The Maple Leafs have won four straight, the latest a 7-2 win at EDM that ended the Oilers' three-game streak and saw William Nylander reach 300 career goals. They're still without John Tavares (lower body), and Colton Sissons has taken his spot beside Nylander and Gavin McKenna. The Flames have won three straight, most recently 4-1 over DET, and Mikael Backlund is day-to-day and could return.

Both teams are being outchanced more often than not at five on five, with TOR at 45% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and CGY at 47%. Toronto's results run ahead of its chances, helped by finishing and goaltending. Calgary's last five show the same gap: only 46% of the expected goals, held up by goaltending. The Flames take 4.6 penalties a game, and Toronto's power play and Calgary's penalty kill both rate close to even. In net, projected starters Sergei Bobrovsky (+3.3 goals saved above expected, a measure of saves beyond what the shots warranted) and Dustin Wolf (-8.0) are going in opposite directions this season, though Bobrovsky was at -13.5 last year.

Auston Matthews, one point from 800 career points, is 39% to score and 69% for a point. Nylander is 38% to score and 73% for a point. Our under-the-radar picks are Calgary's Morgan Frost, a third-liner whose shots have been dangerous lately (24% to score), and Matt Coronato, 57% for a point on a line that creates chances. Both are players to watch, not locks.
